text:
AI fluency grows through practical builds: Cam's Tech Thursday recap puts a human story behind starting small.
Make one explainable change, check it, then take the next step.
Follow Layer8Culture for the work behind the demo.

Copilot browser use: test the form, not just the screenshot.

What changed: GitHub announced browser use in public preview on Nov. 17, connecting Copilot to Chrome through an extension.

What it does: browser interaction, real-time web-app debugging and browser testing from supported Copilot clients.

Builder value: the website build discussed on Tech Thursday at 23:49-24:14 is the starting point. Checking whether a person can finish a task is the next experiment, not a result we're claiming from that episode.

Try this week:
1. Install GitHub's Copilot Chrome extension and enable browser use in your supported client. In CLI, find it under /plugin, enable it, then start a new session. Check the extension says Connected.
2. Use a localhost page with dummy data. Ask: 'Submit this form with a required field empty. Report what happens; do not edit files.'
3. Inspect the result yourself. If you request a fix, review the diff and rerun the same test. Keep deployment behind human approval.

The signal: AI work is extending from writing the page into checking the experience. A successful click is still not proof of a correct workflow.

Source: GitHub Changelog, Nov. 17, 'Let GitHub Copilot interact with your browser.' Public preview; availability and policies may vary.

Save this for your next AI-built page.
